title: Microfeedback morning brief and request genealogy
content:
Purpose
Quick morning brief for the field and product partners: compile raw asks we heard last week, show how they relate (request genealogy), and propose <low-touch> experiments we can spin up this sprint. Goal is to reduce duplicate tickets + create 2 rapid probes that reduce friction for top-of-stack customers.

Method & assumptions
- Sources: support threads, CSM calls (Dec 18–29), live onboarding sessions, and a small set of enterprise health check interviews.
- ‘Genealogy’ = parent request (root pain) -> derived asks (workarounds, feature asks, policy requests).
- Triage lens: safety of customer (security/compliance), business impact (ARR signal), implementation effort (S/M/L).
- This doc intentionally focuses on small, reversible experiments (UI toggles, prompt+policy tweaks, routing alias, telemetry flag) rather than heavy infra changes.

Topline summary (one paragraph)
Customers continue to surface three clusters: 1) predictable tail-latency and inconsistent fallbacks when a model variant is out of capacity (enterprise, high-throughput customers), 2) embedding drift and index staleness for long-lived retrieval apps (customers using Dedicated and Private), and 3) prompt safety/structured-output regressions after model rollouts (notably in chat-with-tools flows). Many asks are surface symptoms of routing, versioning, and visibility gaps — which is why the request genealogy is helpful: several small fixes (clearer route insights + per-route fallback policy + an embed-reindex scheduler UI) would reduce multiple tickets.

Representative customer quotes
- "We saw a 4–8s spike for a small fraction of calls when the Primary pool spilled — there was no obvious reason in the console why that shard failed." — Fintech PLT, Tier 1
- "Embeddings drifted after our weekly content push; similarity search returned old answers for weeks until we manually reindexed." — Knowledge base vendor
- "After the chat model update, our structured JSON outputs broke in 3 places; rollback was manual and painful." — Marketplace app

Request genealogy (high level examples)
1) Root: unpredictable spillover / capacity mismatch
   - Derived ask A: Console visibility: per-request routing path + pool id (easy wins)
   - Derived ask B: Auto-fallback policy by latency threshold (S)
   - Derived ask C: Deeper: autoscale rules tuned by seq-len histogram (M)

2) Root: embedding index staleness
   - Derived ask A: Scheduled reindex UI (S)
   - Derived ask B: Realtime partial refresh for small patches (M)
   - Derived ask C: Reindex cost estimator and dry-run preview (M)

3) Root: rollout regressions in structured outputs
   - Derived ask A: Canary set and schema-guard evals (S)
   - Derived ask B: Prompt-suite regression alerts (S)
   - Derived ask C: Per-version deterministic fallback + auto-rollback (L)

Clusters & prioritized fragments (why these matter)
- Latency & fallback cluster (priority: high for a small set of enterprise customers). Business impact: timeouts -> revenue loss. Common friction: console traces are too coarse; no route-id visible in logs.
- Embeddings & indexing cluster (priority: medium, broad surface). Business impact: semantic search regressions -> UX break. Common friction: lack of schedule + cost estimate for reindex.
- Structured-output regressions (priority: high for heavy chat customers using tool-calling). Business impact: incorrect data sent to downstream systems; trust loss.

Proposed low-touch experiments (pick 2 this sprint)
1) Console route-inspector flag (S) — owner: Luca Romano
   - What: Add an opt-in per-API-key toggle that surfaces routing path, selected pool, and model-variant id for each request in the Console.
   - Why: reduces mean time to diagnose spillover by giving immediate evidence of fallback events.
   - Acceptance criteria: customers in pilot see >50% reduction in time-to-closure for related support tickets.
   - Effort: S (console front-end + short telemetry flag).

2) Reindex-scheduler MVP (S) — owner: Maya Thompson
   - What: Simple scheduled job UI where a user can pick a cadence (daily/weekly) and an estimated token-cost shown before scheduling.
   - Why: addresses many reindexing tickets and reduces ad-hoc manual reindex requests.
   - Acceptance criteria: pilot customer uses scheduler for one content push and reports no manual reindex within 30 days.
   - Effort: S (UI + backend job trigger + basic RBAC).

3) Canary prompt-suite + schema guard (S) — owner: Owen Chen (solutions)
   - What: Allow teams to assign a small canary percentage of traffic to new model versions with a per-prompt evaluation harness that checks structural schema and a few golden patterns.
   - Why: detect structured-output regressions before full rollout.
   - Acceptance criteria: detect at least one schema regression in a rollout test (simulated).

Ticket mapping (quick links / example JIRA keys)
- JIRA-CS-1423 => Fleet of tickets about missing route-id in logs
- JIRA-EMB-210 => Reindex automation requests from three customers
- JIRA-ROLL-55 => Rollout regression case from Marketplace app

Open questions / risks (notes to product teams)
- Are we comfortable surfacing pool/variant ids to customers at the level proposed? security implication for hosted models? (ask security & legal).
- Reindex cost estimation accuracy for large corpora — needs a small pilot to calibrate.
- Canary harness needs to hook into existing eval infra; who owns the golden prompt-suite?

Quick next steps (this week)
- Sync T/Th with infra + security to validate route-inspector data exposure (Aisha)
- Spin up a small pilot for reindex scheduler with KB vendor (Maya)
- Draft a canary prompt-suite template and circulate to 2 product teams (Owen)
- Create JIRA epic to centralize the three S experiments: JIRA-EPIC-630 (owner: Aisha)

Notes / scratchpad (informal)
- If we do 1) and 2) we probably reduce ~30% of the related tickets across top 10 customers. Back-of-envelope ARR impact TODO.
- Some customers asked for per-route cost breakdown by token -> could be a follow-up to the route-inspector design.
- Keep experiments reversible and opt-in; we should avoid any automatic reindex without explicit confirmation.

Unresolved items to capture in a follow-up short doc
- Security review outcome for route-id exposure (deadline: Jan 20)
- Reindex cost calculator accuracy report (deadline: Jan 28)
- Canary harness integration plan with rollout infra (deadline: Feb 3)

If you want to run a quick field-check before the Friday sync, I can compile 6–8 raw snippets per cluster and share a preview slate for the Product Weekly. Mark items you want me to expand into a full PRD.

-- Aisha (CS lead)
